title: Tomato Soup with Basil Oil
description: Silky roasted-tomato soup finished with bright green basil oil.
source: Sample recipe — replace with the real version from a starred chat

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss tomatoes, onion, and garlic with olive oil and a big pinch of salt on a sheet pan, cut sides up.
Roast until the edges char and the tomatoes collapse, about 30 minutes.
steps.why: Charring isn't burning — it's caramelization and Maillard browning driving off water and building deep roasted sweetness. Crushing raw tomatoes into a pot gives you acid with none of that roundness.

steps.text: Meanwhile, make the basil oil: blanch basil in boiling water for 10 seconds, shock in ice water, squeeze bone dry.
steps.why: Ten seconds of heat kills the enzymes that would turn the oil muddy brown, and the ice shock locks the chlorophyll bright green.

steps.text: Blend the basil with the neutral oil and a pinch of salt until vivid green, about 45 seconds. Strain through a fine sieve without pressing.
steps.why: Pressing the solids forces fine particles through and clouds the oil — let gravity work and you get a jewel-clear green.

steps.text: Blend the roasted vegetables with the stock until completely smooth. Work in batches and leave the blender lid vented.
steps.why: Hot liquid in a sealed blender builds steam pressure and erupts. Venting lets it escape.

steps.text: Return to the pot, warm gently, and stir in the cream if using. Season — it usually wants more salt than you think and a crack of pepper.

notes.title: Make ahead
notes.body: The soup holds 3 days refrigerated. The basil oil stays vividly green about 2 days — store them separately and rewarm gently.

plating: Wide shallow bowls. Pour the soup, then spoon basil oil in a broken ring — it should pool in emerald islands, not blend in. One basil leaf dead center.
variations: Add a parmesan rind while the soup warms for extra depth (remove before serving).
